name: CISSP dump (reviewed) - Domain 1: Security and Risk Management

questions.stem: A company whose Information Technology (IT) services are being delivered from a Tier 4 data center, is preparing a companywide Business Continuity Planning (BCP). Which of the following failures should the IT manager be concerned with?
options: Application
Storage
Power
Network
questions.explanation: A Tier 4 facility already provides fault-tolerant power, storage paths and network; the application layer remains the IT manager's own concern.
optionNotes: Correct: application failures are not mitigated by Tier 4 facility redundancy.
Tier 4 provides redundant storage paths/systems.
Tier 4 guarantees redundant, fault-tolerant power.
Tier 4 has redundant network carriers and paths.

questions.stem: Intellectual property rights are PRIMARILY concerned with which of the following?
options: Owner's ability to realize financial gain
Owner's ability to maintain copyright
Right of the owner to enjoy their creation
Right of the owner to control delivery method
questions.explanation: Intellectual property law primarily protects the owner's ability to profit from the creation.
optionNotes: Correct: IP law exists mainly to let owners profit.
Copyright is one IP mechanism, not the purpose.
Enjoyment is not the legal focus of IP rights.
Delivery control is incidental, not primary.

questions.stem: All of the following items should be included in a Business Impact Analysis (BIA) questionnaire EXCEPT questions that
options: determine the risk of a business interruption occurring
determine the technological dependence of the business processes
Identify the operational impacts of a business interruption
Identify the financial impacts of a business interruption
questions.explanation: A BIA measures impacts and dependencies, not likelihood; likelihood belongs to risk assessment.
optionNotes: Correct: likelihood is risk assessment, not BIA.
BIA does capture technology dependencies.
Operational impact is core BIA content.
Financial impact is core BIA content.

questions.stem: An important principle of defense in depth is that achieving information security requires a balanced focus on which PRIMARY elements?
options: Development, testing, and deployment
Prevention, detection, and remediation
People, technology, and operations
Certification, accreditation, and monitoring
questions.explanation: Defense in depth (NSA model) balances people, technology and operations.
optionNotes: SDLC stages, not defense-in-depth elements.
Control functions, not the DiD balance elements.
Correct: NSA DiD focuses on people, technology, operations.
Authorization lifecycle steps, not DiD.

questions.stem: Which of the following is an initial consideration when developing an information security management system?
options: Identify the contractual security obligations that apply to the organizations
Understand the value of the information assets
Identify the level of residual risk that is tolerable to management
Identify relevant legislative and regulatory compliance requirements
questions.explanation: Valuing information assets is the starting point for scoping an ISMS and its controls.
optionNotes: Contract obligations are inputs later in scoping.
Correct: asset value drives the ISMS scope and protection.
Risk tolerance is set after assets are valued.
Legal requirements matter but follow asset understanding.

questions.stem: An organization is found lacking the ability to properly establish performance indicators for its Web hosting solution during an audit. What would be the MOST probable cause?
options: Absence of a Business Intelligence (BI) solution
Inadequate cost modeling
Improper deployment of the Service-Oriented Architecture (SOA)
Insufficient Service Level Agreement (SLA)
questions.explanation: Performance indicators for a hosted service come from the SLA; an insufficient SLA is the likely cause.
optionNotes: BI solution isn't required for KPIs.
Cost modeling isn't performance metrics.
SOA deployment is unrelated.
Correct: SLAs define performance indicators.

questions.stem: A Business Continuity Plan/Disaster Recovery Plan (BCP/DRP) will provide which of the following?
options: Guaranteed recovery of all business functions
Minimization of the need for decision making during a crisis
Insurance against litigation following a disaster
Protection from loss of organization resources
questions.explanation: BCP/DRP pre-defines procedures and roles so fewer ad hoc decisions are needed in a crisis. Guarantees of full recovery or protection from all loss are impossible, and plans do not shield against litigation. What a plan realistically delivers is pre-decided actions, so stressed staff improvise less.
optionNotes: No plan can guarantee recovery of everything.
Right: pre-made procedures and roles reduce crisis decision-making.
Plans do not insure against lawsuits.
Plans reduce impact but cannot prevent loss of resources.

questions.stem: Which of the following types of business continuity tests includes assessment of resilience to internal and external risks without endangering live operations?
options: Walkthrough
Simulation
Parallel
White box
questions.explanation: A simulation exercises responses to a realistic scenario without affecting production systems. A walkthrough only reviews the plan on paper, and a parallel test actually activates recovery sites. A simulation is the option that tests resilience to a scenario while live operations stay untouched.
optionNotes: Walkthrough is a discussion review of the plan, not a scenario assessment.
Right: simulation runs a scenario against risks without touching operations.
Parallel test activates alternate systems; heavier and resource intensive.
White box is a software/pen test term, not a BC test type.

questions.stem: Recovery strategies of a Disaster Recovery planning (DRP) MUST be aligned with which of the following?
options: Hardware and software compatibility issues
Applications' criticality and downtime tolerance
Budget constraints and requirements
Cost/benefit analysis and business objectives
questions.explanation: Recovery strategies must be justified by cost/benefit and support business objectives, as decided by management. Application criticality and downtime tolerance (B) are BIA inputs, but management selects recovery strategies by weighing cost against benefit. That keeps recovery spending proportional to business value.
optionNotes: Compatibility is a technical detail, not the alignment driver.
Criticality/tolerance feed the BIA but strategies must be business-justified overall.
Budget alone is one constraint, not the full alignment.
Right: strategies must be cost-justified and support business objectives.

questions.stem: What security management control is MOST often broken by collusion?
options: Job rotation
Separation of duties
Least privilege model
Increased monitoring
questions.explanation: Collusion is the way separation of duties is defeated. Job rotation (A) is a control that helps uncover collusion rather than one it defeats. Separation of duties assumes no single person can complete a sensitive task, and collusion bypasses exactly that.
optionNotes: Job rotation helps detect collusion rather than being broken by it.
Right: collusion is two or more people defeating separation of duties.
Least privilege is broken by excess rights, not primarily collusion.
Monitoring is a detective control, not the one collusion defeats.

questions.stem: A security consultant has been asked to research an organization's legal obligations to protect privacy-related information. What kind of reading material is MOST relevant to this project?
options: The organization's current security policies concerning privacy issues
Privacy-related regulations enforced by governing bodies applicable to the organization
Privacy best practices published by recognized security standards organizations
Organizational procedures designed to protect privacy information
questions.explanation: Legal obligations come from applicable laws/regulations, not internal policy or best practice. Policies and procedures (A, D) may be incomplete, and best practices (C) are not binding. Legal obligations come from the laws and regulations that apply to the organization.
optionNotes: Current policy may not reflect legal obligations.
Right: legal obligations are set by applicable laws and regulators.
Best practices are not legal obligations.
Procedures implement policy, not law.

questions.stem: Which of the following elements MUST a compliant EU-US Safe Harbor Privacy Policy contain?
options: An explanation of how long the data subject's collected information will be retained for and how it will be eventually disposed.
An explanation of who can be contacted at the organization collecting the information if corrections are required by the data subject.
An explanation of the regulatory frameworks and compliance standards the information collecting organization adheres to.
An explanation of all the technologies employed by the collecting organization in gathering information on the data subject.
questions.explanation: Safe Harbor principles included access: subjects must be able to contact the organization to correct data. The Safe Harbor principles required notice, including how individuals could contact the organization, plus access rights to correct their data. The other items were not mandatory contents.
optionNotes: Retention detail was not a mandated element.
Right: Safe Harbor required notice of contact and access/correction rights.
Listing frameworks was not required.
Describing all technologies was not required.

questions.stem: In Business Continuity Planning (BCP), what is the importance of documenting business processes?
options: Provides senior management with decision-making tools
Establishes and adopts ongoing testing and maintenance strategies
Defines who will perform which functions during a disaster or emergency
Provides an understanding of the organization's interdependencies
questions.explanation: Documenting processes reveals dependencies between functions, systems and resources. Assigning roles (C) comes from the plan itself. Mapping business processes shows which functions depend on which systems, people and suppliers, and that feeds the BIA.
optionNotes: Decision tools come from the BIA overall, not process docs.
Testing/maintenance strategy is separate from process documentation.
Role assignment comes from the plan, not process docs.
Right: process documentation reveals interdependencies.

questions.stem: Which type of control recognizes that a transaction amount is excessive in accordance with corporate policy?
options: Detection
Prevention
Investigation
Correction
questions.explanation: Recognizing (flagging) an excessive amount is a detective control. A preventive control (B) would block the transaction outright. Recognizing or flagging an amount that exceeds policy is a detective function.
optionNotes: Right: identifying an excessive amount after it occurs is detective.
Prevention would block the transaction outright.
Investigation is not a control category here.
Correction restores after an issue.

questions.stem: Copyright provides protection for which of the following?
options: Ideas expressed in literary works
A particular expression of an idea
New and non-obvious inventions
Discoveries of natural phenomena
questions.explanation: Copyright protects an author's particular expression of an idea once fixed in a tangible form. The underlying idea stays free for others to express differently.
optionNotes: Ideas themselves are never copyrightable; only their expression
Right: copyright covers the specific expression
Novel, non-obvious inventions are patent territory
Natural phenomena cannot be owned under any IP regime

questions.stem: Which of the following is the BEST mitigation from phishing attacks?
options: Network activity monitoring
Security awareness training
Corporate policy and procedures
Strong file and directory permissions
questions.explanation: Phishing exploits human trust rather than a technical flaw. Training users to recognise and report suspicious messages directly reduces the chance they click or disclose credentials, making it the best mitigation.
optionNotes: Monitoring may detect consequences but does not stop users being deceived
Right: targets the human weakness phishing exploits
Policy sets rules but does not by itself teach recognition
Permissions do not prevent credential theft via deception

questions.stem: The PRIMARY purpose of a security awareness program is to
options: ensure that everyone understands the organization's policies and procedures.
communicate that access to information will be granted on a need-to-know basis.
warn all users that access to all systems will be monitored on a daily basis.
comply with regulations related to data and information protection.
questions.explanation: Awareness programs aim to make every staff member understand the organisation's security policies and procedures and their own responsibilities. Messages about monitoring or need-to-know are content within that goal, not its purpose.
optionNotes: Right: shared understanding of policies is the purpose
Need-to-know is an access principle, one topic among many
Monitoring notice is a deterrent message, not the primary goal
Regulatory compliance is a by-product, not the main purpose

questions.stem: When constructing an Information Protection Policy (IPP), it is important that the stated rules are necessary, adequate, and
options: flexible.
confidential.
focused.
achievable.
questions.explanation: Policy rules must be necessary, adequate and achievable. A rule people cannot realistically follow breeds non-compliance and undermines the whole policy.
optionNotes: Too much flexibility weakens enforceability
Policies must be communicated to staff, not kept secret
'Focused' is vague and not the standard criterion
Right: rules must be attainable to be followed

questions.stem: Which of the following MUST be part of a contract to support electronic discovery of data stored in a cloud environment?
options: Integration with organizational directory services for authentication
Tokenization of data
Accommodation of hybrid deployment models
Identification of data location
questions.explanation: E-discovery requires locating and preserving relevant data, and in the cloud data location also determines jurisdiction. The contract must therefore require the provider to identify where data is stored.
optionNotes: Directory integration is an authentication matter
Tokenisation is a protection technique, not discovery support
Hybrid deployment support is architectural
Right: location knowledge enables discovery and legal hold

questions.stem: Which of the following is the MAIN reason that system re-certification and re-accreditation are needed?
options: To assist data owners in making future sensitivity and criticality determinations
To assure the software development team that all security issues have been addressed
To verify that security protection remains acceptable to the organizational security policy
To help the security team accept or reject new systems for implementation and production
questions.explanation: Systems, threats and policies change over time. Periodic recertification and reaccreditation confirm the protection still meets policy and that residual risk is still acceptable.
optionNotes: Classification decisions are the data owner's separate task
Assurance to developers is not the purpose
Right: confirms ongoing acceptability
Initial accreditation covers new systems

questions.stem: Which of the following is the MOST important consideration when storing and processing Personally Identifiable Information (PII)?
options: Encrypt and hash all PII to avoid disclosure and tampering.
Store PII for no more than one year.
Avoid storing PII in a Cloud Service Provider.
Adherence to collection limitation laws and regulations.
questions.explanation: Handling PII must above all meet legal and regulatory obligations such as collection limitation. Technical choices like encryption follow from those obligations.
optionNotes: Hashing PII destroys usability; encryption is a control, not the top consideration
Arbitrary retention period not grounded in law
Cloud storage can be compliant
Right: legal compliance governs PII handling

questions.stem: While impersonating an Information Security Officer (ISO), an attacker obtains information from company employees about their User IDs and passwords. Which method of information gathering has the attacker used?
options: Trusted path
Malicious logic
Social engineering
Passive misuse
questions.explanation: Impersonating a trusted official to trick employees into revealing credentials is social engineering.
optionNotes: Trusted path is a secure user-to-TCB channel, not an attack
Malicious logic means malware code, not pretexting
Pretexting as a trusted officer to elicit passwords is social engineering
Passive misuse is not a recognised term for this deception

questions.stem: An organization is selecting a service provider to assist in the consolidation of multiple computing sites including development, implementation and ongoing support of various computer systems. Which of the following MUST be verified by the Information Security Department?
options: The service provider's policies are consistent with ISO/IEC27001 and there is evidence that the service provider is following those policies.
The service provider will segregate the data within its systems and ensure that each region's policies are met.
The service provider will impose controls and protections that meet or exceed the current systems controls and produce audit logs as verification.
The service provider's policies can meet the requirements imposed by the new environment even if they differ from the organization's current policies.
questions.explanation: When outsourcing, security must ensure the provider's controls are at least as strong as the existing ones and are verifiable via audit evidence.
optionNotes: ISO alignment alone doesn't prove equivalent control strength
Data segregation is only one narrow requirement
Controls must equal or exceed current ones with audit-log evidence
Accepting differing policies may lower the protection level

questions.stem: The use of strong authentication, the encryption of Personally Identifiable Information (PII) on database servers, application security reviews, and the encryption of data transmitted across networks provide
options: data integrity.
defense in depth.
data availability.
non-repudiation.
questions.explanation: Multiple overlapping controls at different layers is defense in depth.
optionNotes: Integrity is only one facet; the controls are layered
Multiple independent layers across identity, data, app and network
These controls don't target uptime
No signatures are involved to give non-repudiation

questions.stem: An internal Service Level Agreement (SLA) covering security is signed by senior managers and is in place. When should compliance to the SLA be reviewed to ensure that a good security posture is being delivered?
options: As part of the SLA renewal process
Prior to a planned security audit
Immediately after a security breach
At regularly scheduled meetings
questions.explanation: SLA compliance should be monitored routinely through regularly scheduled reviews, not only at renewal or after incidents.
optionNotes: Renewal-only review lets non-compliance persist for the term
Pre-audit review is ad hoc
Post-breach review is reactive
Scheduled periodic reviews give continuous assurance

questions.stem: Which of the following MUST be done when promoting a security awareness program to senior management?
options: Show the need for security; identify the message and the audience
Ensure that the security presentation is designed to be all-inclusive
Notify them that their compliance is mandatory
Explain how hackers have enhanced information security
questions.explanation: To win management support, show the business need for security and identify the message and target audience.
optionNotes: Demonstrating need and targeting message/audience wins management buy-in
All-inclusive design is not a requirement
Telling senior management compliance is mandatory won't gain support
Hackers haven't 'enhanced' security; off-message

questions.stem: Refer to the information below to answer the question. An organization has hired an information security officer to lead their security department. The officer has adequate people resources but is lacking the other necessary components to have an effective security program. There are numerous initiatives requiring security involvement. Given the number of priorities, which of the following will MOST likely influence the selection of top initiatives?
options: Severity of risk
Complexity of strategy
Frequency of incidents
Ongoing awareness
questions.explanation: Initiatives are prioritized by risk severity.
optionNotes: Risk severity ranks which initiatives to address first
Strategy complexity doesn't set priority
Incident frequency is one input to risk, not the criterion
Awareness is a program element, not a selection driver

questions.stem: Refer to the information below to answer the question. An organization has hired an information security officer to lead their security department. The officer has adequate people resources but is lacking the other necessary components to have an effective security program. There are numerous initiatives requiring security involvement. Which of the following is considered the MOST important priority for the information security officer?
options: Formal acceptance of the security strategy
Disciplinary actions taken against unethical behavior
Development of an awareness program for new employees
Audit of all organization system configurations for faults
questions.explanation: Senior management formal acceptance of the security strategy is the foundation for all other program work.
optionNotes: Management's formal acceptance of strategy is the foundation
Disciplinary actions are operational, later
Awareness programs follow an approved strategy
Configuration audits are tactical, later

questions.stem: During an audit, the auditor finds evidence of potentially illegal activity. Which of the following is the MOST appropriate action to take?
options: Immediately call the police
Work with the client to resolve the issue internally
Advise the person performing the illegal activity to cease and desist
Work with the client to report the activity to the appropriate authority
questions.explanation: An auditor should work with the client to report illegal activity to the proper authorities, following due process.
optionNotes: Calling police directly bypasses the client and engagement terms
Resolving internally may conceal illegal activity
Confronting the person may tip them off and destroy evidence
Reporting jointly with the client follows due process

questions.stem: Refer to the information below to answer the question. An organization experiencing a negative financial impact is forced to reduce budgets and the number of Information Technology (IT) operations staff performing basic logical access security administration functions. Security processes have been tightly integrated into normal IT operations and are not separate and distinct roles. Which of the following will be the PRIMARY security concern as staff is released from the organization?
options: Inadequate IT support
Loss of data and separation of duties
Undocumented security controls
Additional responsibilities for remaining staff
questions.explanation: When integrated security staff are cut, the people who performed access administration leave with knowledge and privileges, and remaining staff absorb conflicting duties. The primary security concern is therefore loss of data and erosion of separation of duties.
optionNotes: Operational support issue, not the primary security concern.
Correct: departing staff risk data loss and remaining staff accumulate incompatible duties.
Possible but secondary; controls may still exist even if poorly documented.
A workload consequence; the security impact is the SoD breakdown it causes.

questions.stem: A risk assessment report recommends upgrading all perimeter firewalls to mitigate a particular finding. Which of the following BEST supports this recommendation?
options: The inherent risk is greater than the residual risk.
The Annualized Loss Expectancy (ALE) approaches zero.
The expected loss from the risk exceeds mitigation costs.
The infrastructure budget can easily cover the upgrade costs.
questions.explanation: A control is justified when its cost is less than the loss it prevents, which is a cost/benefit analysis. Budget availability or inherent vs residual risk alone do not justify a specific spend.
optionNotes: Always true for any control; does not justify this one.
An ALE near zero would argue against spending.
Correct: expected loss exceeding mitigation cost is the classic justification.
Affordability is not a risk-based justification.

questions.stem: A Business Continuity Plan (BCP) is based on
options: the policy and procedures manual.
an existing BCP from a similar organization.
a review of the business processes and procedures.
a standard checklist of required items and objectives.
questions.explanation: A BCP is built on the business impact analysis, which comes from reviewing the organization's own business processes and their dependencies. Templates or another organization's plan do not reflect its critical functions.
optionNotes: Manuals help but do not identify critical processes.
Another organization's plan will not match this business.
Correct: the plan derives from analysis of the organization's processes.
Checklists support but cannot replace process analysis.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a BEST practice when traveling internationally with laptops containing Personally Identifiable Information (PII)?
options: Use a thumb drive to transfer information from a foreign computer.
Do not take unnecessary information, including sensitive information.
Connect the laptop only to well-known networks like the hotel or public Internet cafes.
Request international points of contact help scan the laptop on arrival to ensure it is protected.
questions.explanation: The safest approach when travelling with PII is data minimisation: carry only what is necessary. Devices may be inspected, seized or stolen at borders, so less data means less exposure.
optionNotes: Foreign computers and thumb drives introduce malware and data-leak risk.
Correct: not carrying unnecessary sensitive data minimizes exposure.
Hotel and cafe networks are untrusted.
Handing the laptop to others increases exposure.

questions.stem: Refer to the information below to answer the question. An organization has hired an information security officer to lead their security department. The officer has adequate people resources but is lacking the other necessary components to have an effective security program. There are numerous initiatives requiring security involvement. The effectiveness of the security program can PRIMARILY be measured through
options: audit findings.
risk elimination.
audit requirements.
customer satisfaction.
questions.explanation: An effective program is evidenced by independent assessment of control performance. Audit findings show objectively whether controls are working; risk can never be eliminated.
optionNotes: Correct: audit findings objectively measure control effectiveness.
Risk elimination is impossible.
Requirements define what is audited, not results.
Satisfaction is subjective and not a security measure.

questions.stem: Refer to the information below to answer the question. An organization experiencing a negative financial impact is forced to reduce budgets and the number of Information Technology (IT) operations staff performing basic logical access security administration functions. Security processes have been tightly integrated into normal IT operations and are not separate and distinct roles. When determining appropriate resource allocation, which of the following is MOST important to monitor?
options: Number of system compromises
Number of audit findings
Number of staff reductions
Number of additional assets
questions.explanation: After cuts, management must know whether the reduced staff can still protect the environment. Tracking the number of system compromises gives a direct indicator of whether security resourcing is adequate.
optionNotes: Correct: compromises show whether reduced resources are failing to protect assets.
Audit findings lag and reflect compliance rather than actual protection.
Staff reductions are an input, not an outcome to monitor.
Asset growth affects workload but does not measure effectiveness.

questions.stem: Refer to the information below to answer the question. An organization has hired an information security officer to lead their security department. The officer has adequate people resources but is lacking the other necessary components to have an effective security program. There are numerous initiatives requiring security involvement. The security program can be considered effective when
options: vulnerabilities are proactively identified.
audits are regularly performed and reviewed.
backups are regularly performed and validated.
risk is lowered to an acceptable level.
questions.explanation: Security exists to manage risk to a level acceptable to management. A program is effective when risk has been reduced to that acceptable level, not simply when activities occur.
optionNotes: An activity, not proof of effectiveness.
Audits are activities; performing them does not show effectiveness.
A narrow operational control.
Correct: reducing risk to an acceptable level is the goal.

questions.stem: Refer to the information below to answer the question. During the investigation of a security incident, it is determined that an unauthorized individual accessed a system which hosts a database containing financial information. If it is discovered that large quantities of information have been copied by the unauthorized individual, what attribute of the data has been compromised?
options: Availability
Integrity
Accountability
Confidentiality
questions.explanation: Copying information without authorization exposes it to unauthorized parties, which is a loss of confidentiality.
optionNotes: Data remains available.
Copying does not alter data.
Not a core data attribute affected here.
Correct: unauthorized disclosure is a confidentiality breach.

questions.stem: Refer to the information below to answer the question. A large organization uses unique identifiers and requires them at the start of every system session. Application access is based on job classification. The organization is subject to periodic independent reviews of access controls and violations. The organization uses wired and wireless networks and remote access. The organization also uses secure connections to branch offices and secure backup and recovery strategies for selected information and processes. Following best practice, where should the permitted access for each department and job classification combination be specified?
options: Security procedures
Security standards
Human resource policy
Human resource standards
questions.explanation: Mandatory, specific requirements such as permitted access for each department and job class belong in security standards, which support policy. Procedures describe how to perform tasks.
optionNotes: Procedures are step-by-step instructions, not access specifications.
Correct: standards give mandatory specific requirements such as role access.
HR policy does not define system access.
HR standards cover personnel matters, not access rules.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a detective access control mechanism?
options: Log review
Least privilege
Password complexity
Non-disclosure agreement
questions.explanation: Detective controls identify events after they occur. Reviewing logs uncovers violations; the others are preventive or deterrent.
optionNotes: Correct: log review detects incidents.
Least privilege is preventive.
Password complexity is preventive.
NDAs are deterrent/administrative.

questions.stem: Refer to the information below to answer the question. A large, multinational organization has decided to outsource a portion of their Information Technology (IT) organization to a third-party provider's facility. This provider will be responsible for the design, development, testing, and support of several critical, customer-based applications used by the organization. The organization should ensure that the third party's physical security controls are in place so that they
options: are more rigorous than the original controls.
are able to limit access to sensitive information.
allow access by the organization staff at any time.
cannot be accessed by subcontractors of the third party.
questions.explanation: When development and support of critical applications is outsourced, the provider's physical controls must restrict access to the organization's sensitive information.
optionNotes: More rigor is not required; adequacy is.
Correct: physical controls must limit access to sensitive data.
Unrestricted access is not a control goal.
Subcontractors may be permitted under contract.

questions.stem: A security manager has noticed an inconsistent application of server security controls resulting in vulnerabilities on critical systems. What is the MOST likely cause of this issue?
options: A lack of baseline standards
Improper documentation of security guidelines
A poorly designed security policy communication program
Host-based Intrusion Prevention System (HIPS) policies are ineffective
questions.explanation: Without baseline standards defining required server configurations, controls get applied inconsistently. Baselines provide the mandatory minimum configuration.
optionNotes: Right: no baseline means each admin configures differently.
Guidelines are optional, so they don't enforce consistency anyway.
Communication matters less than having a mandatory standard.
HIPS covers only one control and doesn't explain wider inconsistency.

questions.stem: Refer to the information below to answer the question. During the investigation of a security incident, it is determined that an unauthorized individual accessed a system which hosts a database containing financial information. If the intrusion causes the system processes to hang, which of the following has been affected?
options: System integrity
System availability
System confidentiality
System auditability
questions.explanation: Hanging processes prevent the system from serving users, which is a loss of availability.
optionNotes: Integrity concerns unauthorized modification, not hangs.
Right: hung processes deny service, so availability is hit.
Confidentiality is disclosure, not hangs.
Auditability isn't a CIA effect of hung processes.

questions.stem: An organization publishes and periodically updates its employee policies in a file on their intranet. Which of the following is a PRIMARY security concern?
options: Availability
Confidentiality
Integrity
Ownership
questions.explanation: Policies published for employees must be accurate and authoritative, so unauthorized modification (integrity) is the primary concern.
optionNotes: Availability matters but stale access is a lesser risk.
Policies are published internally and aren't secret.
Right: tampered policies would mislead employees.
Ownership isn't a security concern here.

questions.stem: Refer to the information below to answer the question. A large, multinational organization has decided to outsource a portion of their Information Technology (IT) organization to a third-party provider's facility. This provider will be responsible for the design, development, testing, and support of several critical, customer-based applications used by the organization. What additional considerations are there if the third party is located in a different country?
options: The organizational structure of the third party and how it may impact timelines within the organization
The ability of the third party to respond to the organization in a timely manner and with accurate information
The effects of transborder data flows and customer expectations regarding the storage or processing of their data
The quantity of data that must be provided to the third party and how it is to be used
questions.explanation: Offshore outsourcing raises transborder data flow laws and customer expectations about where their data is stored or processed.
optionNotes: Org structure affects any vendor, foreign or not.
Responsiveness applies to any vendor.
Right: cross-border data laws and customer expectations are country-specific.
Data quantity matters with any vendor.

questions.stem: A business has implemented Payment Card Industry Data Security Standard (PCI-DSS) compliant handheld credit card processing on their Wireless Local Area Network (WLAN) topology. The network team partitioned the WLAN to create a private segment for credit card processing using a firewall to control device access and route traffic to the card processor on the Internet. What components are in the scope of PCI-DSS?
options: The entire enterprise network infrastructure.
The handheld devices, wireless access points and border gateway.
The end devices, wireless access points, WLAN, switches, management console, and firewall.
The end devices, wireless access points, WLAN, switches, management console, and Internet
questions.explanation: PCI DSS scope covers every component that stores, processes, transmits or connects to cardholder data, including the segment's devices, APs, WLAN, switches, management console and the firewall that segments it.
optionNotes: Proper segmentation means the whole network is out of scope.
Leaves out switches, management console and segmenting firewall.
Right: everything in or connected to the cardholder segment, including the firewall.
The Internet is outside the entity's control and scope.

questions.stem: Refer to the information below to answer the question. An organization experiencing a negative financial impact is forced to reduce budgets and the number of Information Technology (IT) operations staff performing basic logical access security administration functions. Security processes have been tightly integrated into normal IT operations and are not separate and distinct roles. Which of the following will indicate where the IT budget is BEST allocated during this time?
options: Policies
Frameworks
Metrics
Guidelines
questions.explanation: Metrics show where controls perform and where risk lies, so they guide where to put limited budget.
optionNotes: Policies set direction but don't measure where to spend.
Frameworks structure the program but don't show performance.
Right: metrics show control effectiveness and risk to guide spend.
Guidelines are optional advice.

questions.stem: When dealing with compliance with the Payment Card Industry-Data Security Standard (PCI-DSS), an organization that shares card holder information with a service provider MUST do which of the following?
options: Perform a service provider PCI-DSS assessment on a yearly basis.
Validate the service provider's PCI-DSS compliance status on a regular basis.
Validate that the service providers security policies are in alignment with those of the organization.
Ensure that the service provider updates and tests its Disaster Recovery Plan (DRP) on a yearly basis.
questions.explanation: PCI DSS requires the entity to monitor its service providers' compliance status at least annually.
optionNotes: Doing the provider's assessment yourself isn't required.
Right: PCI DSS requires monitoring provider compliance status.
Policy alignment isn't the PCI requirement.
DRP testing isn't the PCI third-party requirement.

questions.stem: Refer to the information below to answer the question. A new employee is given a laptop computer with full administrator access. This employee does not have a personal computer at home and has a child that uses the computer to send and receive e-mail, search the web, and use instant messaging. The organization's Information Technology (IT) department discovers that a peer-to-peer program has been installed on the computer using the employee's access. Which of the following documents explains the proper use of the organization's assets?
options: Human resources policy
Acceptable use policy
Code of ethics
Access control policy
questions.explanation: The acceptable use policy defines proper use of organizational assets.
optionNotes: The HR policy covers employment, not asset use.
Right: the AUP defines proper use of organizational assets.
The code of ethics covers conduct broadly.
The access control policy covers authorization rules.

questions.stem: Which of the following MOST influences the design of the organization's electronic monitoring policies?
options: Workplace privacy laws
Level of organizational trust
Results of background checks
Business ethical considerations
questions.explanation: Monitoring policy must first comply with applicable workplace privacy laws.
optionNotes: Right: privacy laws limit and shape what monitoring is allowed.
Trust is cultural and comes second to law.
Background checks are unrelated to monitoring design.
Ethics matter but law is the binding constraint.

questions.stem: What is the PRIMARY reason for ethics awareness and related policy implementation?
options: It affects the workflow of an organization.
It affects the reputation of an organization.
It affects the retention rate of employees.
It affects the morale of the employees.
questions.explanation: Ethics programs mainly protect the organization's reputation and public trust.
optionNotes: Workflow isn't the main driver.
Right: ethics lapses damage reputation and trust.
Retention is a secondary effect.
Morale is a secondary effect.

questions.stem: What is the MOST critical factor to achieve the goals of a security program?
options: Capabilities of security resources
Executive management support
Effectiveness of security management
Budget approved for security resources
questions.explanation: Executive management support is the most critical success factor for a security program; it drives funding, authority and culture.
optionNotes: Staff capability matters but depends on support.
Right: senior management support drives everything else.
Effective management requires mandate from the top.
Budget follows executive support.

questions.stem: Which of the following countermeasures is the MOST effective in defending against a social engineering attack?
options: Mandating security policy acceptance
Changing individual behavior
Evaluating security awareness training
Filtering malicious e-mail content
questions.explanation: Social engineering targets people, so the most effective defense is changing how individuals actually behave, usually through awareness programs. Technical filters only cover some channels.
optionNotes: Signing a policy does not change behavior
Behavior change addresses the human weakness being exploited
Evaluating training measures it but is not itself the countermeasure
Email filtering covers only one attack channel

questions.stem: When evaluating third-party applications, which of the following is the GREATEST responsibility of Information Security?
options: Accept the risk on behalf of the organization.
Report findings to the business to determine security gaps.
Quantify the risk to the business for product selection.
Approve the application that best meets security requirements.
questions.explanation: Security's role is to advise: it quantifies risk so business owners can make informed product selection decisions. Accepting risk and approving purchases belong to the business.
optionNotes: Risk acceptance belongs to management/business owners
Reporting gaps is weaker than quantifying risk for decision-making
Quantifying risk enables an informed business choice
Approval is a business decision, not security's

questions.stem: The MAIN reason an organization conducts a security authorization process is to
options: force the organization to make conscious risk decisions.
assure the effectiveness of security controls.
assure the correct security organization exists.
force the organization to enlist management support.
questions.explanation: Authorization (ATO) requires a senior official to formally decide whether to accept residual risk. It forces conscious risk decisions.
optionNotes: The core purpose is an explicit risk acceptance decision
Assessment verifies controls; authorization is the decision
Organizational structure is not the goal
Management support is a by-product

questions.stem: Which of the following is the BEST example of weak management commitment to the protection of security assets and resources?
options: poor governance over security processes and procedures
immature security controls and procedures
variances against regulatory requirements
unanticipated increases in security incidents and threats
questions.explanation: Weak governance over security processes directly reflects lack of management commitment.
optionNotes: Poor governance directly shows lacking management commitment
Immaturity can stem from resources or time
Regulatory variances may have other causes
Incident increases can be external, not commitment-related

questions.stem: Determining outage costs caused by a disaster can BEST be measured by the
options: cost of redundant systems and backups.
cost to recover from an outage.
overall long-term impact of the outage.
revenue lost during the outage.
questions.explanation: Outage cost is best measured by the overall long-term impact, including reputation and lost business, not only immediate costs.
optionNotes: Redundancy cost is a mitigation cost, not outage cost
Recovery cost is only part of the loss
Long-term impact captures total loss including reputation
Lost revenue is only the immediate loss

questions.stem: What does the Maximum Tolerable Downtime (MTD) determine?
options: The estimated period of time a business critical database can remain down before customers are affected.
The fixed length of time a company can endure a disaster without any Disaster Recovery (DR) planning
The estimated period of time a business can remain interrupted beyond which it risks never recovering
The fixed length of time in a DR process before redundant systems are engaged
questions.explanation: MTD is the longest a business can be interrupted before the outage threatens its survival.
optionNotes: Limited to one database and customers, too narrow
MTD is not about absence of DR planning
Maximum interruption before survival is threatened
Failover timing relates to RTO, not MTD

questions.stem: In order for a security policy to be effective within an organization, it MUST include
options: strong statements that clearly define the problem.
a list of all standards that apply to the policy.
owner information and date of last revision.
disciplinary measures for non compliance.
questions.explanation: Without consequences for non-compliance, policy has no enforcement and is ineffective.
optionNotes: Problem statements alone do not drive compliance
Standards are referenced separately, not required in policy
Ownership info is administrative, not effectiveness
Consequences give policy enforceability

questions.stem: A database administrator is asked by a high-ranking member of management to perform specific changes to the accounting system database. The administrator is specifically instructed to not track or evidence the change in a ticket. Which of the following is the BEST course of action?
options: Ignore the request and do not perform the change.
Perform the change as requested, and rely on the next audit to detect and report the situation.
Perform the change, but create a change ticket regardless to ensure there is complete traceability.
Inform the audit committee or internal audit directly using the corporate whistleblower process.
questions.explanation: An instruction to bypass change controls on a financial system suggests possible fraud and should be escalated through independent whistleblower channels.
optionNotes: Silently refusing leaves possible fraud unreported
Performing untracked changes breaks change control
Still performs a possibly fraudulent change
Independent escalation through whistleblowing is proper

questions.stem: The goal of a Business Continuity Plan (BCP) training and awareness program is to
options: enhance the skills required to create, maintain, and execute the plan.
provide for a high level of recovery in case of disaster.
describe the recovery organization to new employees.
provide each recovery team with checklists and procedures.
questions.explanation: BCP training builds the skills people need to create, maintain and execute the plan.
optionNotes: Builds skills to create, maintain and execute the plan
Recovery level depends on the plan, not training goal
Orientation of new staff is too narrow
Checklists are plan content, not training goals

questions.stem: An organization's information security strategic plan MUST be reviewed
options: whenever there are significant changes to a major application.
quarterly, when the organization's strategic plan is updated.
whenever there are major changes to the business.
every three years, when the organization's strategic plan is updated.
questions.explanation: A security strategic plan supports business strategy, so it must be revisited when the business itself changes substantially. Fixed calendar cycles or single application changes do not drive strategic review.
optionNotes: One application change is tactical, not strategic.
Fixed quarterly timing ignores event-driven need; strategy is rarely quarterly.
Right: major business change invalidates strategic assumptions.
Three-year cycle is too rigid for strategic alignment.

questions.stem: Backup information that is critical to the organization is identified through a
options: Vulnerability Assessment (VA).
Business Continuity Plan (BCP).
Business Impact Analysis (BIA).
data recovery analysis.
questions.explanation: [Key corrected: book said B] The BIA identifies critical business processes and the data and resources they depend on, which tells you which backup information is critical. The BCP is built from those BIA results.
optionNotes: VA finds weaknesses, not business criticality.
BCP consumes BIA output rather than identifying criticality.
Right: BIA determines criticality of processes and data.
Not a standard method for establishing criticality.

questions.stem: The goal of a Business Impact Analysis (BIA) is to determine which of the following?
options: Cost effectiveness of business recovery
Cost effectiveness of installing software security patches
Resource priorities for recovery and Maximum Tolerable Downtime (MTD)
Which security measures should be implemented
questions.explanation: A BIA determines how disruptions affect the business, producing MTD/RTO values and recovery priorities. Cost-effectiveness and control selection come later in continuity planning.
optionNotes: Recovery cost analysis follows the BIA.
Patching cost is unrelated to BIA.
Right: BIA yields MTD and recovery priorities.
Control selection is risk treatment, not BIA.

questions.stem: Are companies legally required to report all data breaches?
options: No, different jurisdictions have different rules.
No, not if the data is encrypted.
No, companies' codes of ethics don't require it.
No, only if the breach had a material impact.
questions.explanation: Breach notification duties come from many state, national and sector laws with differing triggers. So whether a report is required depends on the jurisdiction.
optionNotes: Right: rules vary by jurisdiction.
Encryption safe harbors exist only in some laws.
Ethics codes are irrelevant to legal duty.
Materiality thresholds are not universal.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the BEST method to reduce the effectiveness of phishing attacks?
options: User awareness
Two-factor authentication
Anti-phishing software
Periodic vulnerability scan
questions.explanation: Phishing targets people, so awareness training that teaches users to recognise and report it reduces its success most broadly. Technical tools help but cannot catch every lure.
optionNotes: Right: users are the target and last line of defence.
2FA limits credential reuse but not malware or other phishing goals.
Filters miss novel phishing.
Scanning finds system flaws, not social engineering.

questions.stem: Which of the following restricts the ability of an individual to carry out all the steps of a particular process?
options: Job rotation
Separation of duties
Least privilege
Mandatory vacations
questions.explanation: Separation of duties splits a critical process among people so no one can complete it alone. That prevents fraud without collusion.
optionNotes: Rotation moves people between jobs to detect fraud.
Right: divides process steps among individuals.
Least privilege limits rights, not process steps.
Vacations help detect fraud after the fact.

questions.stem: The application of which of the following standards would BEST reduce the potential for data breaches?
options: ISO 9000
questions.explanation: ISO 27001 specifies an information security management system, which directly addresses data breach risk. The others are quality, events and social responsibility.
optionNotes: Quality management.
Event sustainability.
Social responsibility.
Right: ISMS for information security.

questions.stem: A company was ranked as high in the following National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) functions: Protect, Detect, Respond and Recover. However, a low maturity grade was attributed to the Identify function. In which of the following the controls categories does this company need to improve when analyzing its processes individually?
options: Asset Management, Business Environment, Governance and Risk Assessment
Access Control, Awareness and Training, Data Security and Maintenance
Anomalies and Events, Security Continuous Monitoring and Detection Processes
Recovery Planning, Improvements and Communications
questions.explanation: In the NIST CSF (v1.1), the Identify function has the categories Asset Management, Business Environment, Governance, Risk Assessment and Risk Management Strategy. Those are where the company must improve.
optionNotes: Right: Identify categories.
Protect categories.
Detect categories.
Recover categories.

questions.stem: The World Trade Organization's (WTO) agreement on Trade-Related Aspects of Intellectual Property Rights (TRIPS) requires authors of computer software to be given the
options: right to refuse or permit commercial rentals.
right to disguise the software's geographic origin.
ability to tailor security parameters based on location.
ability to confirm license authenticity of their works.
questions.explanation: TRIPS Article 11 gives authors of computer programs the right to authorize or prohibit commercial rental of their works. It is a specific rental right.
optionNotes: Correct: TRIPS grants rental rights for software.
Disguising origin has nothing to do with TRIPS.
Location-based security parameters are not an IP right.
License authenticity checking is not a TRIPS-granted right.

questions.stem: How can lessons learned from business continuity training and actual recovery incidents BEST be used?
options: As a means for improvement
As alternative options for awareness and training
As indicators of a need for policy
As business function gap indicators
questions.explanation: Lessons learned exist to feed continuous improvement of the BC plan and program. They highlight what to fix in plans, training and procedures.
optionNotes: Correct: lessons learned drive improvement.
Awareness is one possible use, not the best overall one.
Lessons may show a policy gap, but improvement is broader.
Gap indication is narrower than overall improvement.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the BEST approach to take in order to effectively incorporate the concepts of business continuity into the organization?
options: Ensure end users are aware of the planning activities
Validate all regulatory requirements are known and fully documented
Develop training and awareness programs that involve all stakeholders
Ensure plans do not violate the organization's cultural objectives and goals
questions.explanation: Embedding BC in the organization's culture takes training and awareness that involve all stakeholders. Then everyone understands their role and the plan becomes part of normal operations.
optionNotes: Awareness only for end users is too narrow.
Regulatory documentation is compliance, not culture.
Correct: involving all stakeholders through training builds BC into the organization.
Cultural alignment is a constraint, not the method.

questions.stem: What is the PRIMARY difference between security policies and security procedures?
options: Policies are used to enforce violations, and procedures create penalties
Policies point to guidelines, and procedures are more contractual in nature
Policies are included in awareness training, and procedures give guidance
Policies are generic in nature, and procedures contain operational details
questions.explanation: Policies are high-level, mandatory statements of intent. Procedures are detailed step-by-step instructions for carrying them out.
optionNotes: Neither policies nor procedures 'enforce violations' or create penalties.
Policies do not merely point to guidelines, and procedures are not contracts.
Both can appear in training; that is not the difference.
Correct: policies are generic, procedures operational.

questions.stem: Which of the following standards/guidelines requires an Information Security Management System (ISMS) to be defined?
options: International Organization for Standardization (ISO) 27000 family
Information Technology Infrastructure Library (ITIL)
Payment Card Industry Data Security Standard (PCIDSS)
ISO/IEC 20000
questions.explanation: ISO/IEC 27001, part of the 27000 family, requires an organization to establish, implement, maintain and improve an ISMS.
optionNotes: Correct: the ISO 27000 family defines ISMS requirements.
ITIL is an IT service management framework.
PCI DSS sets cardholder data controls, not an ISMS.
ISO 20000 is a service management system standard.

questions.stem: Which of the following has the GREATEST impact on an organization's security posture?
options: International and country-specific compliance requirements
Security violations by employees and contractors
Resource constraints due to increasing costs of supporting security
Audit findings related to employee access and permissions process
questions.explanation: External compliance obligations drive the controls an organization must implement across all operations, so they shape the overall security posture most broadly. The other items are individual events or constraints that affect parts of the program.
optionNotes: Correct: mandatory legal/regulatory requirements shape the entire security program.
Violations are incidents that reflect posture rather than define it.
Resource constraints limit but do not set the posture.
Audit findings on one process are narrow in scope.

questions.stem: What does an organization FIRST review to assure compliance with privacy requirements?
options: Best practices
Business objectives
Legal and regulatory mandates
Employee's compliance to policies and standards
questions.explanation: Privacy compliance starts with knowing what the law and regulators require; everything else is measured against those mandates.
optionNotes: Best practices are optional guidance.
Business objectives do not define privacy obligations.
Correct: legal/regulatory mandates define compliance.
Employee compliance is checked later against policies derived from mandates.

questions.stem: During the risk assessment phase of the project the CISO discovered that a college within the University is collecting Protected Health Information (PHI) data via an application that was developed in-house. The college collecting this data is fully aware of the regulations for Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA) and is fully compliant. What is the best approach for the CISO? During the risk assessment phase of the project the CISO discovered that a college within the University is collecting Protected Health Information (PHI) data via an application that was developed in-house. The college collecting this data is fully aware of the regulations for Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA) and is fully compliant. What is the best approach for the CISO?
options: Document the system as high risk
Perform a vulnerability assessment
Perform a quantitative threat assessment
Notate the information and move on
questions.explanation: The college already knows and complies with HIPAA, so the risk is already addressed by the responsible owner. During risk assessment the CISO records the finding and continues rather than duplicating controls.
optionNotes: Compliant handling does not make it high risk by default.
A vulnerability assessment is not warranted by the facts given.
A quantitative threat assessment is excessive for a compliant system.
Correct: document it and proceed, as it is already compliant.

questions.stem: What is the FIRST step in establishing an information security program?
options: Establish an information security policy.
Identify factors affecting information security.
Establish baseline security controls.
Identify critical security infrastructure.
questions.explanation: A security program is grounded in a policy that shows management intent and authority; standards, baselines and controls derive from it.
optionNotes: Correct: policy establishes the program.
Identifying factors is input but policy sets direction.
Baselines derive from policy.
Infrastructure identification follows policy.

questions.stem: Who would be the BEST person to approve an organizations information security policy?
options: Chief Information Officer (CIO)
Chief Information Security Officer (CISO)
Chief internal auditor
Chief Executive Officer (CEO)
questions.explanation: [Key corrected: book said B] Senior management carries ultimate responsibility for security and approves the policy; the CISO writes and maintains it.
optionNotes: CIO is an IT executive, not top authority.
CISO drafts but should not approve.
Auditors must stay independent.
Correct: CEO/senior management approves.

questions.stem: A control to protect from a Denial-of-Service (DoS) attack has been determined to stop 50% of attacks, and additionally reduces the impact of an attack by 50%. What is the residual risk?
questions.explanation: Only half of attacks succeed, and those have half the impact: 0.5 x 0.5 = 0.25, so 25% of original risk remains.
optionNotes: Correct: 50% x 50% = 25%.
50% ignores the impact reduction.
75% would be the reduction amount.
100% ignores the control.

questions.stem: An Information Technology (IT) professional attends a cybersecurity seminar on current incident response methodologies. What code of ethics canon is being observed?
options: Provide diligent and competent service to principals
Protect society, the commonwealth, and the infrastructure
Advance and protect the profession
Act honorably, honestly, justly, responsibly, and legally
questions.explanation: OSG10 ties canon IV, Advance and protect the profession, to keeping your knowledge current and adding to the shared body of knowledge. Going to a seminar on current incident-response methods is that kind of professional development. Canon III is about the service you give to principals, not about building your own skills.
optionNotes: Wrong: canon III is about competent, unbiased service to principals, not learning.
Wrong: canon I is about protecting society and infrastructure.
Right: OSG10 links keeping knowledge current to canon IV.
Wrong: canon II is about honourable, legal conduct.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a direct monetary cost of a security incident?
options: Morale
Reputation
Equipment
Information
questions.explanation: Equipment replacement is a direct, quantifiable monetary cost; morale, reputation and information value are indirect or intangible.
optionNotes: Morale loss is an indirect, intangible impact
Reputational damage is indirect and hard to quantify
Correct: replacing or repairing equipment is a direct cash cost
Information value is an asset impact, not a direct outlay

questions.stem: A security professional determines that a number of outsourcing contracts inherited from a previous merger do not adhere to the current security requirements. Which of the following BEST minimizes the risk of this happening again?
options: Define additional security controls directly after the merger
Include a procurement officer in the merger team
Verify all contracts before a merger occurs
Assign a compliancy officer to review the merger conditions
questions.explanation: Reviewing contracts for security compliance before a merger is a preventive control that stops non-compliant obligations from being inherited.
optionNotes: Reactive: acts only after bad contracts are inherited
A procurement officer lacks a security-compliance remit
Correct: pre-merger contract due diligence stops the problem recurring
Merger conditions differ from reviewing each outsourcing contract

questions.stem: Who has the PRIMARY responsibility to ensure that security objectives are aligned with organization goals?
options: Senior management
Information security department
Audit committee
All users
questions.explanation: Senior management aligns security with business goals through governance.
optionNotes: Correct: governance and alignment are senior management's responsibility
Security implements, it doesn't own alignment
The audit committee provides oversight, not alignment
Users follow policy; they don't set alignment

questions.stem: What is the MAIN goal of information security awareness and training?
options: To inform users of the latest malware threats
To inform users of information assurance responsibilities
To comply with the organization information security policy
To prepare students for certification
questions.explanation: Awareness makes users understand their security and information-assurance responsibilities.
optionNotes: Malware news is content, not the main goal
Correct: users must understand their security responsibilities
Compliance is a by-product
Certification prep is professional education, not awareness

questions.stem: Which of the following is the BEST reason for writing an information security policy?
options: To support information security governance
To reduce the number of audit findings
To deter attackers
To implement effective information security controls
questions.explanation: Policy is the foundation of security governance, setting management intent and direction.
optionNotes: Correct: policy expresses management direction, which is the basis of governance
Fewer audit findings is a side effect
Policies don't deter attackers
Controls come from standards and procedures derived from policy

questions.stem: An organization plan on purchasing a custom software product developed by a small vendor to support its business model. Which unique consideration should be made part of the contractual agreement potential long-term risks associated with creating this dependency?
options: A source code escrow clause
Right to request an independent review of the software source code
Due diligence form requesting statements of compliance with security requirements
Access to the technical documentation
questions.explanation: Source code escrow protects the buyer if a small vendor fails or stops supporting the product.
optionNotes: Correct: escrow gives source access if the vendor fails
A code review checks quality, not continuity
Compliance statements don't address vendor failure
Documentation without source can't sustain the product

questions.stem: What are the steps of a risk assessment?
options: identification, analysis, evaluation
analysis, evaluation, mitigation
classification, identification, risk management
identification, evaluation, mitigation
questions.explanation: ISO 31000 defines risk assessment as risk identification, analysis and evaluation.
optionNotes: Correct: ISO 31000 defines assessment as identification, analysis and evaluation
Mitigation is treatment, not assessment
Classification is not a step
Analysis is missing; mitigation is treatment

questions.stem: Which of the following is the MOST challenging issue in apprehending cyber criminals?
options: They often use sophisticated method to commit a crime.
It is often hard to collect and maintain integrity of digital evidence.
The crime is often committed from a different jurisdiction.
There is often no physical evidence involved.
questions.explanation: Cross-jurisdiction issues are the hardest obstacle to apprehending cyber criminals.
optionNotes: Sophistication can be countered by skill
Evidence handling is hard but manageable
Correct: different jurisdictions block arrest and extradition
Lack of physical evidence is common and manageable

questions.stem: An organization has outsourced its financial transaction processing to a Cloud Service Provider (CSP) who will provide them with Software as a Service (SaaS). If there was a data breach who is responsible for monetary losses?
options: The Data Protection Authority (DPA)
The Cloud Service Provider (CSP)
The application developers
The data owner
questions.explanation: The data owner stays accountable for losses; responsibility cannot be outsourced.
optionNotes: A DPA regulates; it is not liable
The CSP may be contractually liable, but ultimate accountability stays with the owner
Developers aren't accountable
Correct: the data owner remains accountable for losses

questions.stem: When determining who can accept the risk associated with a vulnerability, which of the following is the MOST important?
options: Countermeasure effectiveness
Type of potential loss
Incident likelihood
Information ownership
questions.explanation: Only the information owner can accept risk for their assets.
optionNotes: Effectiveness affects residual risk, not who accepts it
Loss type informs impact, not authority
Likelihood is a risk input
Correct: the owner of the information has authority to accept risk

questions.stem: An international medical organization with headquarters in the United States (US) and branches in France wants to test a drug in both countries. What is the organization allowed to do with the test subject's data?
options: Aggregate it into one database in the US
Process it in the US, but store the information in France
Share it with a third party
Anonymize it and process it in the US
questions.explanation: EU data protection restricts transfer of personal data; anonymised data is no longer personal data and can be processed in the US.
optionNotes: Transfer of identifiable data restricted
Processing in US is still a transfer
Sharing needs a lawful basis/consent
Correct: anonymised data is outside GDPR

questions.stem: Attack trees are MOST useful for which of the following?
options: Determining system security scopes
Generating attack libraries
Enumerating threats
Evaluating Denial of Service (DoS) attacks
questions.explanation: Attack trees model the paths to an attacker goal, enumerating threats.
optionNotes: Scoping is set by requirements and boundaries, not attack trees
Attack libraries are catalogues like CAPEC, not the tree's purpose
Correct: trees systematically enumerate the ways a goal can be attacked
DoS is only one possible goal; trees are not DoS-specific

questions.stem: When developing a business case for updating a security program, the security program owner MUST do which of the following?
options: Identify relevant metrics
Prepare performance test reports
Obtain resources for the security program
Interview executive management
questions.explanation: A business case needs measurable metrics to justify the investment.
optionNotes: Correct
Not required
Result of approval
Helpful, not mandatory

questions.stem: What is the expected outcome of security awareness in support of a security awareness program?
options: Awareness activities should be used to focus on security concerns and respond to those concerns accordingly
Awareness is not an activity or part of the training but rather a state of persistence to support the program
Awareness is training. The purpose of awareness presentations is to broaden attention of security.
Awareness is not training. The purpose of awareness presentation is simply to focus attention on security.
questions.explanation: Awareness is distinct from training; it focuses attention on security.
optionNotes: Responding to concerns is an incident/feedback activity, not awareness's outcome
Awareness is an activity, so this is false
Awareness is explicitly distinguished from training
Correct: awareness focuses attention on security

questions.stem: Which of the following mandates the amount and complexity of security controls applied to a security risk?
options: Security vulnerabilities
Risk tolerance
Risk mitigation
Security staff
questions.explanation: Risk tolerance dictates how much control is needed.
optionNotes: Vulnerabilities are inputs to risk analysis, not the deciding factor
Correct: management's tolerance sets how far risk must be reduced
Mitigation is the result of the decision, not its driver
Staff availability limits implementation but does not mandate control level

questions.stem: Which of the following is the MOST important activity an organization performs to ensure that security is part of the overall organization culture?
options: Ensure security policies are issued to all employees
Perform formal reviews of security Incidents.
Manage a program of security audits.
Work with senior management to meet business goals.
questions.explanation: Aligning security with business goals through senior management embeds it in culture.
optionNotes: Issuing policies alone does not create culture
Incident reviews are reactive and limited
Audits drive compliance, not culture
Correct: alignment with business goals via senior management embeds security

questions.stem: An organization outgrew its internal data center and is evaluating third-party hosting facilities. In this evaluation, which of the following is a PRIMARY factor for selection?
options: Facility provides an acceptable level of risk
Facility provides disaster recovery (DR) services
Facility provides the most cost-effective solution
Facility has physical access protection measures
questions.explanation: Selection should be driven by whether residual risk is acceptable to the organization. Cost, DR and physical controls all feed into that risk judgement.
optionNotes: Acceptable risk is the overarching selection criterion.
DR services are one factor within risk.
Cost alone must not override risk.
Physical protection is one control within risk.

questions.stem: The acquisition of personal data being obtained by a lawful and fair means is an example of what principle?
options: Data Quality Principle
Openness Principle
Purpose Specification Principle
Collection Limitation Principle
questions.explanation: OECD Collection Limitation requires data be obtained by lawful and fair means. It also says collection should be with the subject's knowledge or consent where appropriate.
optionNotes: Data quality concerns accuracy and relevance.
Openness concerns transparency of practices.
Purpose specification concerns stated purposes.
Collection limitation requires lawful, fair means of collection.

questions.stem: When designing a business continuity plan (BCP), what is the formula to determine the Maximum Tolerable Downtime (MTD)?
options: Annual Loss Expectancy (ALE) + Work Recovery Time (WRT)
Business impact analysis (BIA) + Recovery Point Objective (RPO)
Recovery Time Objective (RTO) + Work Recovery Time (WRT)
Estimated Maximum Loss (EML) + Recovery Time Objective (RTO)
questions.explanation: MTD = RTO + WRT. WRT covers verifying and restoring data after systems recover.
optionNotes: ALE is financial, not time.
BIA is a process, RPO is data loss.
MTD = RTO + WRT.
EML is financial.

questions.stem: What is the FIRST step in risk management?
options: Establish the expectations of stakeholder involvement.
Identify the factors that have potential to impact business.
Establish the scope and actions required.
Identify existing controls in the environment.
questions.explanation: Risk management starts by framing the context: setting the scope and boundaries and what the process must accomplish. Identifying factors and controls only happens once the scope is set.
optionNotes: Stakeholder expectations are part of context but narrower.
Identifying impact factors is risk identification, which comes after scoping.
Right: establishing scope comes first.
Inventorying existing controls is part of the assessment, later.

questions.stem: What is the FIRST step for an organization to take before allowing personnel to access social media from a corporate device or user account?
options: Publish a social media guidelines document.
Publish an acceptable usage policy.
Document a procedure for accessing social media sites.
Deliver security awareness training.
questions.explanation: Policy comes first: an acceptable use policy sets the rules for using corporate devices and accounts on social media. Guidelines, procedures and training follow from that policy.
optionNotes: Guidelines are non-mandatory and come after policy.
Right: the AUP is the first, foundational step.
Procedures implement policy and come later.
Training communicates the policy after it exists.

questions.stem: What is the MOST effective way to determine a mission critical asset in an organization?
options: Vulnerability analysis
business process analysis
Threat analysis
Business risk analysis
questions.explanation: Analysing business processes shows which processes the mission depends on and therefore which supporting assets are mission-critical. Threat and vulnerability analysis assess risk to assets but don't establish how critical they are.
optionNotes: Vulnerability analysis finds weaknesses, not criticality.
Right: business process analysis identifies mission-critical assets.
Threat analysis identifies threats, not asset importance.
Risk analysis builds on criticality that has already been determined.

questions.stem: The adoption of an enterprise-wide Business Continuity (BC) program requires which of the following?
options: Good communication throughout the organization
A completed Business Impact Analysis (BIA)
Formation of Disaster Recovery (DR) project team
Well-documented information asset classification
questions.explanation: An enterprise-wide BC program depends on awareness and buy-in across all business units, which requires good communication throughout the organization. The BIA and team formation are steps inside the program rather than requirements for adopting it.
optionNotes: Right: enterprise adoption depends on organization-wide communication.
The BIA is performed within the program once it is adopted.
The DR team is a component formed during the program.
Asset classification is helpful but not required for adopting BC.

questions.stem: Which of the following BEST describes the objectives of the Business Impact Analysis (BIA)?
